finding.preliminary_assessment: filterCollisions() iterates over the fields array using an index that reads fields.length on each iteration. When splitField() is called (line 110), it returns [f1, f2] which are concatenated to the fields array via fields.concat(). Because the outer loop reads fields.length dynamically, the two new split fields are immediately queued for processing. If a server sends 1000 overlapping transformation rectangles for a single field, each split produces 2 more fields which are also processed — in the worst case this creates O(n) or worse growth. For 1000 overlapping rects: approximately 2000+ fields processed. Combined with VULN-006 (null pointer dereference), a compromised ApplinX backend could chain these to cause a browser-side denial of service by sending a screen response with many overlapping regionsToHide for fields with null content.

patterns_observed: Array mutation during iteration — fields.concat() grows array while loop uses dynamic length
No maximum field count limit per input field
No maximum transformation rectangle count per screen
VULN-006 (null content) and VULN-012 (unbounded growth) can be chained for compounded DoS

false_positives.rationale: Growth is linear per split (2 fields per split), not exponential — but 1000 overlapping rects still produces 2000+ iterations, which may be sufficient for DoS

analysis.coverage_assessment: Complete analysis of filterCollisions() including the loop structure, concat behavior, and interaction with splitField/cutField.

for_inquisitor: Test with 100, 1000, and 10000 overlapping rectangles — measure browser performance impact
Verify if ApplinX REST API has server-side limits on transformation rectangle count per field
Evaluate fix: add a maximum fields count check (e.g., if fields.length > MAX_FIELDS break)
Assess whether this is exploitable via a compromised ApplinX backend vs normal operational conditions
